This page covers the exact U.S. O*NET/SOC occupation 49-9041.00, Industrial Machinery Mechanics: repairing, installing, adjusting, or maintaining industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems, and possibly installing, dismantling, or moving machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. Official scope: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. U.S. wages and employment come from BLS OEWS 2025 and BLS employment projections for 2024–2034 as presented by O*NET (the exact 49-9041.00 occupation). Exact mainland Chinese occupational wages were not obtained and are recorded as a visible gap. No fully equivalent unified mainland Chinese occupational qualification was obtained; check region, equipment type, and company procedures. The two jurisdictions' legal and safety systems cannot be applied interchangeably.

To assess your fit for industrial machinery maintenance, first complete a verifiable repair exercise using public or simulated materials. Define a fictional equipment failure, such as an unexpected production-line machinery shutdown. Write a step-by-step workflow covering work-permit and safety-isolation confirmation, observation and anomaly identification, disassembly and parts inspection, fault diagnosis, component repair or replacement, reassembly and testing, and repair and maintenance documentation. Mark each step's checkpoints and possible problems: missing safety isolation or lockout/tagout, incorrect part specifications or misjudged excessive wear, incorrect disassembly or assembly sequence, tests missing critical operating conditions, or unauthorized equipment modification. Then check whether safety isolation and lockout/tagout, parts and specification checks, and test verification are indispensable; whether equipment modifications, engineering judgments, and safety determinations beyond your authority are escalated or referred; and whether repairs and maintenance leave reviewable records. Test yourself through a concrete deliverable rather than relying solely on an interest questionnaire.

Fit signals | U.S. O*NET 49-9041.00 tasks and work activities show that this occupation centers on repairing or maintaining production and processing machinery, repairing or replacing faulty components, cleaning, lubricating and adjusting, disassembling and reassembling, inspecting parts for defects, documenting repairs and maintenance, and operating machinery to verify repairs. Work is primarily at equipment sites, requiring protective equipment and work around contaminants, hazardous equipment, and noise. The interest code is RCI (Realistic–Conventional–Investigative). Key skills include equipment maintenance, operation and control, operations monitoring, repairing, and troubleshooting. If you are willing to perform hands-on site repairs according to procedures, value safety and precision, and accept defined job responsibilities, these daily requirements may align with your working style.

Caution signals | The official scope and tasks involve equipment sites, safety isolation, and inspection judgments. Missing safety isolation or lockout/tagout, incorrect part specifications or wear assessment, an incorrect disassembly or assembly sequence, tests missing critical operating conditions, or unauthorized equipment modification can cause injury, equipment damage, or production stoppage. This page therefore addresses safety isolation and protection, parts and specification checks, disassembly and test verification, and authorization boundaries separately. The U.S. occupation is designated Bright Outlook. O*NET's summary and employment trends indicate much faster-than-average projected growth of 16% for 2024–2034, about 45,700 annual openings, and about 439,600 people employed in 2024. If site conditions, exposure to contaminants and hazardous equipment, or shift work are difficult for you, weigh these practical costs carefully.

Taking responsibility | Fit depends on whether you can do three things within the same repair task: substantiate the repair (confirm permits, observe and inspect, disassemble and diagnose, repair or replace, reassemble and test, and produce reviewable repair records); uphold standards and safety (safety isolation and lockout/tagout, parts and specification checks, and protective equipment under organizational and regulatory requirements); and accept defined job responsibilities (take responsibility for your repair quality and records, while escalating or referring equipment modifications, engineering judgments, and safety determinations beyond your authority). Test this through a verifiable experience, such as producing a step-by-step repair workflow and diagnostic record or practicing identification and response with simulated equipment anomalies, rather than relying only on an interest questionnaire.

Industrial machinery mechanics' daily work can be divided into three streams: (1) safety and preparation—confirm work permits and safety isolation, apply lockout/tagout, wear protective equipment, and study drawings and manufacturers' manuals; (2) repair and diagnosis—observe and identify anomalies, disassemble and inspect parts for defects, diagnose faults using test equipment, and repair or replace components; and (3) assembly and verification—reassemble in sequence, operate equipment to verify repairs, document repairs and maintenance, and order required parts. All three share safety and quality requirements but serve different outputs: safety and preparation establish working conditions, repair and diagnosis address root causes, and assembly and verification restore equipment and document results.

O*NET 49-9041.00, Industrial Machinery Mechanics: repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems; may also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. Core tasks include equipment repair and maintenance, component repair or replacement, cleaning, lubrication and adjustment, disassembly, inspection and reassembly, repair documentation and parts ordering, and operation to verify repairs. Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed), SVP range 6.0 to below 7.0. The occupation is designated Bright Outlook.

Industrial machinery mechanics (O*NET/SOC 49-9041.00, Industrial Machinery Mechanics) repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems; they may also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. Official scope: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. Core tasks include repairing or maintaining the operating condition of production and processing machinery or equipment; repairing or replacing broken or malfunctioning components; cleaning, lubricating, or adjusting parts and equipment; disassembling equipment to remove and repair parts; reassembling after inspection, testing, or repair; inspecting parts for breakage or excessive wear; documenting completed repairs and maintenance; and operating newly repaired equipment to verify results. Other tasks include recording and ordering parts and materials, diagnosing faults with test equipment, analyzing test results and machine error messages, studying blueprints or manufacturers' manuals, cutting and welding metal, entering codes to program computer-controlled machinery, demonstrating equipment functions to operators, and assigning work-group schedules. entries.answer: According to O*NET 49-9041.00, this occupation repairs, installs, adjusts, or maintains industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems, and may install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. entries.answer: Machinery maintenance workers focus on routine maintenance and servicing of general machinery; electrical and electronics installers and repairers on electrical and electronic systems; millwrights on equipment installation and alignment; machinists on metal cutting and precision machining; and industrial engineering technologists and technicians on site measurement and data support. subject.name: Industrial Machinery Mechanics
subject.summary: Industrial machinery mechanics correspond to the exact U.S. O*NET/SOC occupation 49-9041.00, Industrial Machinery Mechanics: they repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems, and may also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. Official scope: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans. Core tasks include repairing or maintaining equipment operating condition, repairing or replacing faulty components, cleaning, lubricating and adjusting, disassembling, inspecting and reassembling machinery, inspecting parts for defects, documenting repairs and ordering parts, and operating equipment to verify repairs. U.S. wages and employment on this page come from BLS OEWS 2025 and BLS employment projections for 2024–2034 as presented by O*NET (the exact 49-9041.00 occupation, designated Bright Outlook). Exact occupational wages for mainland China were not obtained and are recorded as a visible gap. No unified Chinese occupational qualification fully equivalent to O*NET 49-9041.00 was obtained either; this gap is recorded under the evidence policy. Chinese safety and special-equipment boundaries are identified separately.
